arxiv-2012-01060.title: Low regularity solutions of two-dimensional compressible Euler equations with dynamic vorticity
arxiv-2012-01060.creator: Huali Zhang
arxiv-2012-01060.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Huali Zhang. By establishing a sharp Strichartz estimate for the velocity and density, we prove the existence, uniqueness, and continuous dependence of solutions for the Cauchy problem of two-dimensional compressible Euler equations, where the initial velocity, density, and specific vorticity ( 𝐯 0 , ρ 0 , ϖ 0 ) ∈ H s ​ ( ℝ 2 ) × H s ​ ( ℝ 2 ) × H 2 ​ ( ℝ 2 ) , s > 7 4 (\mathbf{v}_{0},\rho_{0},\varpi_{0})\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2})\times H^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2}),s>\frac{7}{4} .

arxiv-2106-07635.title: Variational Causal Networks: Approximate Bayesian Inference over Causal Structures
arxiv-2106-07635.creator: Yashas Annadani , Jonas Rothfuss , Alexandre Lacoste , Nino Scherrer , Anirudh Goyal , Yoshua Bengio , Stefan Bauer, ETH Zurich, Mila, Université de Montréal, ElementAI/ ServiceNow, MPI for Intelligent Systems CIFAR Azrieli Global Scholar
arxiv-2106-07635.description: Abstract Learning the causal structure that underlies data is a crucial step towards robust real-world decision making. The majority of existing work in causal inference focuses on determining a single directed acyclic graph (DAG) or a Markov equivalence class thereof.

arxiv-2201-05170.title: ALPINIST: Axion-Like Particles In Numerous Interactions Simulated and Tabulated arXiv: 2201.05170, TTK-22-04, CP3-22-02
arxiv-2201-05170.creator: Jan Jerhot, Babette Döbrich, Fatih Ertas, Felix Kahlhoefer, and Tommaso Spadaro
arxiv-2201-05170.description: Abstract Proton beam dump experiments are among the most promising strategies to search for light and feebly interacting states such as axion-like particles (ALPs). The interpretation of these experiments is however complicated by the wide range of ALP models and the multitude of different production and decay channels that can induce observable signals.

arxiv-2202-06778.title: Gravitational electron-positron scattering
arxiv-2202-06778.creator: W. D. R. Jesus, P. R. A. Souza, A. F. Santos, Faqir C. Khanna
arxiv-2202-06778.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by W. D. R. Jesus, P. R. A. Souza, A. F. Santos, Faqir C. Khanna. A scattering process with gravitons as an intermediate state is investigated. To study such a scattering, the Gravitoelectromagnetism theory is considered. It is a gravitational theory built on the analogy between gravity and electromagnetism. The complete Lagrangian formulation of the gravitoelectromagnetic theory includes interactions of gravitons with fermions and photons that leads us to calculate their scattering amplitudes and cross-sections.

arxiv-2203-08809.title: Broadening the scope of Education, Career and Open Science in HEP
arxiv-2203-08809.creator: Sudhir Malik 1, David DeMuth 2, Sijbrand de Jong 3, Randal Ruchti 4, Savannah Thais 5, Guillermo Fidalgo 1, Ken Heller 6, Mathew Muether 7, Minerba Betancourt 8, Meenakshi Narain 9 Tiffany R. Lewis 10,11, Kyle Cranmer 1,2 and Gordon Watts 1,3
arxiv-2203-08809.description: Abstract High Energy Particle Physics (HEP) faces challenges over the coming decades with a need to attract young people to the field and STEM careers, as well as a need to recognize, promote and sustain those in the field who are making important contributions to the research effort across the many specialties needed to deliver the science.

arxiv-2404-07166.title: Defect-engineering hexagonal boron nitride using low-energy Ar + irradiation
arxiv-2404-07166.creator: Manuel Längle, Barbara Maria Mayer, Jacob Madsen, Diana Propst, Arixin Bo, Clara Kofler, Vinzent Hana, Clemens Mangler, Toma Susi, Jani Kotakoski
arxiv-2404-07166.description: Abstract Monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) has recently become the focus of intense research as a material to host quantum emitters. Although it is well known that such emission is associated with point defects, so far no conclusive correlation between the spectra and specific defects has been demonstrated.

arxiv-2411-11149.title: From Primes to Paths: Enabling Fast Multi-Relational Graph Analysis
arxiv-2411-11149.creator: Konstantinos Bougiatiotis, Georgios Paliouras
arxiv-2411-11149.description: Abstract Multi-relational networks capture intricate relationships in data and have diverse applications across fields such as biomedical, financial, and social sciences. As networks derived from increasingly large datasets become more common, identifying efficient methods for representing and analyzing them becomes crucial.

arxiv-2412-00108.title: Act Now: A Novel Online Forecasting Framework for Large-Scale Streaming Data
arxiv-2412-00108.creator: Daojun Liang 1,5 , Haixia Zhang 2,5 , Jing Wang 3,5 , Dongfeng Yuan 4,5 , Minggao Zhang 2,5
arxiv-2412-00108.description: Abstract In this paper, we find that existing online forecasting methods have the following issues: 1) They do not consider the update frequency of streaming data and directly use labels (future signals) to update the model, leading to information leakage. 2) Eliminating information leakage can exacerbate concept drift and online parameter updates can damage prediction accuracy.

arxiv-2412-15920.title: Data Preparation for Fairness-Performance Trade-Offs: A Practitioner-Friendly Alternative?
arxiv-2412-15920.creator: Gianmario Voria, Rebecca Di Matteo, Giammaria Giordano, Gemma Catolino, Fabio Palomba
arxiv-2412-15920.description: Abstract Context. As machine learning (ML) systems are increasingly adopted across industries, addressing fairness and bias has become essential. While many solutions focus on ethical challenges in ML, recent studies highlight that data itself is a major source of bias. Pre-processing techniques, which mitigate bias before training, are effective but may impact model performance and pose integration difficulties.

pmc-10736022.title: OVERVIEW OF THE NEBRASKA GERIATRIC BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE SURVEY
pmc-10736022.creator: Cecilia Poon
pmc-10736022.description: According to the US Census, more than 16% of Nebraska’s population is 65 and older. Many older Nebraskans reside in rural communities. Although clinicians in existing state-wide workforce surveys endorse working with older adults, it is unclear how frequently they are involved in geriatric mental health.

pmc-11338120.title: Community-level bystander treatment and outcomes for witnessed out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in the state of Connecticut
pmc-11338120.creator: Daniel W Youngstrom, Trevor S Sutton, Fleur S Kabala, Isabella C Rosenzweig, Charles W Johndro, Rabab Al-Araji, Carolyn Burke-Martindale, Jeff F Mather, Raymond G McKay
pmc-11338120.description: Highlights•Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) treatment and outcomes vary significantly by municipality in Connecticut.•Municipality population size greater than 100,000 and predominantly non-English-speaking communities were associated with lower rates of bystander CPR.•Non-English-speaking, low per capita income and Hispanic communities were associated with lower rates of bystander AED use.

pmc-11607046.title: Multi-marker analysis of circulating tumor cells in localized intermediate/high-risk and metastatic prostate cancer
pmc-11607046.creator: Eva Welsch, Lilli Bonstingl, Barbara Holzer, Eva Schuster, Esther Weiß, Alexandru-Teodor Zaharie, Michael Krainer, Michael B. Fischer, Amin El-Heliebi, Robert Zeillinger, Eva Obermayr
pmc-11607046.description: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are an established prognostic marker in metastatic prostate cancer (PrC) but have received little attention in localized high-risk disease. Peripheral blood was obtained from patients with early intermediate and high-risk PrC (n = 15) at baseline, after radiotherapy, and during follow-up, as well as from metastatic PrC patients (n = 23).

pmc-12374978.title: Neural and behavioral reinstatement jointly reflect retrieval of narrative events
pmc-12374978.creator: Matthias Nau, Austin Greene, Hannah Tarder-Stoll, Juan Antonio Lossio-Ventura, Francisco Pereira, Janice Chen, Christopher Baldassano, Chris I Baker
pmc-12374978.description: When recalling past events, patterns of gaze position and neural activity resemble those observed during the original experience. We hypothesized that these two phenomena, known as gaze reinstatement and neural reactivation, are linked through a common process that underlies the reinstatement of past experiences during memory retrieval.

pmc-13024359.title: HDL-Adjusted Inflammatory Ratios and Sequential Graft Configuration are Associated with Mid-Term Saphenous Vein Graft Occlusion in a Post-CABG Angiography Cohort
pmc-13024359.creator: Yusuf Hosoglu, Hakan Tibilli, Veysi Kavalci, Ayşe Hoşoğlu
pmc-13024359.description: BackgroundSaphenous vein graft (SVG) failure limits long-term outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). HDL-adjusted inflammatory ratios, including the neutrophil-to-HDL ratio (NHDLr) and lymphocyte-to-HDL ratio (LHDLr), have emerged as markers of vascular inflammation, but their association with SVG occlusion in the post-CABG setting is unclear.

pmc-13213067.title: Numerical evaluation on behavior of an integrated slope stabilization structure under seismic effect
pmc-13213067.creator: Yujia Wang
pmc-13213067.description: The issue of slope instability is common in the South Gippsland area of Victoria, Australia. To improve the current slope instability circumstance, an integrated slope stabilization structure, which involves two methods, the geogrid-reinforced soil retaining wall with gabion basket facing and the laterally loaded embedded piles, has been adopted.

pmc-13342112.title: Single-molecule kinetic exploration of functional sub-states in an evolving phosphotriesterase
pmc-13342112.creator: Morito Sakuma, Dhani Ram Mahato, Ferran Feixas, Colin J Jackson, Eiji Nakata, Sílvia Osuna, Nobuhiko Tokuriki
pmc-13342112.description: Enzymes can exist in multiple stable functional states or sub-states, revealing substantial molecule-to-molecule heterogeneity in catalytic rates even within populations expressed from a clonal gene. Increasing evidence suggests that biological systems have evolved to exploit these functional sub-states to regulate reaction rates and enzyme multi-functionality or promiscuity.

pmc-13373606.title: Individual patient data meta-analysis and systematic review evaluating camostat mesilate to treat COVID-19
pmc-13373606.creator: Haley Hedlin, Els Tobback, Justin Lee, Yiwen Wang, Ilaria Dragoni, Daniel C. Anthony, Kevin Dhaliwal, John Norrie, Sarah Halford, Jose Gotes, Mariana Moctezuma, Antonio Olivas-Martinez, Chaitan Khosla, Upinder Singh, Jesper Damsgaard Gunst, Alonso Valdez, David Kershenobich, David Boutboul, Ole S. S
pmc-13373606.description: Background:In the COVID-19 pandemic, several phase II and III randomized trials were launched to evaluate the effectiveness of camostat, an orally administered TMPRSS2 inhibitor previously approved for other indications, for treating SARS-CoV-2 infections. Owing to the rapidly changing landscape during the pandemic, many of these trials were unable to reach completion.
